data.narrative:
Qilimanjaro is a Series A quantum computing company that has raised $10M to date. The valuation exercise draws on a comp universe of 11 peers across quantum computing—3 public (IonQ, Rigetti Computing, D-Wave Quantum) and 8 private firms including Quantinuum and Infleqtion.

The Stage-Progression method is the only triangulation approach applicable here. Using total raised ($10M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $20M. The Peer-Median method could not be applied: while 5 same-sector peers exist in the comp universe, none met the filtering criteria for same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with sufficient datapoint density (minimum 3 required), and a broader all-sector median would lack meaningful relevance to frontier-stage quantum technology development.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $17M–$23M, centered on $20M. This range reflects stage-appropriate step-up economics from current capital deployed. Key uncertainties include the absence of directly comparable Series A quantum computing transactions in public records, the nascent commercialization timeline for the sector, and variance in technical differentiation across the peer set. The narrow methodological basis (one applicable approach) underscores execution risk and the need for updated market data as comparable Series A transactions emerge.
